name: Methotrexate
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Methotrexate is excreted mainly unchanged by the kidneys (80% to 90% of an IV dose within 24 hours), so kidney impairment raises levels and toxicity (bone marrow suppression, mucositis), and high doses can themselves cause acute kidney injury. The US label says elimination is reduced below creatinine clearance (CrCl) 90 mL/min and advises considering dose reduction or stopping, without numbers. Dialysis removes it poorly in routine use; glucarpidase is the antidote for toxic levels with delayed clearance.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses Cockcroft-Gault CrCl; reduced elimination below 90 mL/min. No dose bands are given.
chip: Reduce or stop in CKD; label no doses

bands.recommendation: CrCl ≥90: usual dose (RA 7.5 mg once weekly start; psoriasis 10 to 25 mg once weekly). CrCl 60–89: elimination already reduced (label); consider a lower dose and monitor blood counts and creatinine.

Methotrexate elimination falls with CrCl (Cockcroft-Gault) below 90 mL/min and toxicity rises. The label says to consider reducing the dose or stopping it, with no numbers (label 8.6). Low-dose weekly use needs a reduced dose and close blood-count monitoring at most; high-dose regimens need hydration, urine alkalinization, daily levels and leucovorin.

Toxicity risk is high and the label gives no dose; it advises considering discontinuation. Avoid except with specialist decision.

hd: Neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis has been shown to improve elimination; clearance has been reported with acute high-flux hemodialysis (label 10). No maintenance dose in label. Avoid except with specialist decision.
pd: Peritoneal dialysis does not improve elimination (label). Avoid except with specialist decision.
crrt: No data in label; acute kidney injury delays clearance (toxicity). Avoid; for toxic levels use glucarpidase per label. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Moderately by intermittent hemodialysis (EXTRIP 2022), but rapid tissue distribution limits benefit; the label says neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis has been shown to improve elimination, while high-flux hemodialysis has cleared it. EXTRIP recommends glucarpidase rather than extracorporeal removal for severe toxicity.
monitoring: Complete blood count, creatinine (CrCl) and liver tests at baseline and regularly; methotrexate levels with intermediate or high doses; hydration and urine pH ≥7 with high doses. Folic or folinic acid supplementation in RA, pJIA and psoriasis (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, osteosarcoma, meningeal leukemia and polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) (label 8.4).
pediatric.usual_dose: pJIA: 10 mg/m2 once weekly subcutaneously or IM, adjusted to response (label). Oncology: regimen-specific.

renal.recommendation: Label advice is not age-limited: consider dose reduction (no numbers); monitor blood counts and creatinine.
Consider reducing or stopping; specialist input.

adult: JUDGMENT: label gives no numeric kidney doses. CrCl <15, HD, PD and CRRT are red ('avoid unless specialist decision'), which goes beyond the label's 'consider discontinuing'. 15–29 is amber. Dr. Rivero to confirm.
Selected label is the injection (PLR); 11 PH products are 2.5 mg tablets for weekly RA/psoriasis dosing. Weekly (not daily) dosing errors are a key safety point; the tablet label is not stored.
EXTRIP citation verified on PubMed (PMID 35236714; 14 named authors plus a collective-group entry). Its full text is not in PMC; only the abstract was read.
No guideline with numeric low-dose methotrexate kidney cut-offs was verified in this batch.
